source.text: ወማእከላይሰ፡ ይጐድእ፡ እስከ፡ ሰማይ፡ ከመ፡ መንበረ፡ ለእግዚአብሔር፡ ዘእምእብነ፡ ፔካ፡ ወድማሑ፡ ለመንበረ፡ እምእብነ፡ ሰንፔር።
source.note: Same-actor informed corrective-author v3, selected Charles1906 p48 unit8, PDFp86. All13 source words were reaudited against actual primary print, complete photographed Latin entries and grammar. First-word terminal is SatI (ሰ), independently compared as an order to actual TableI, same-font selected sky-first and sapphire-first, and contrasted with same-line eske SatVI. It is not HoiII (ሁ) or the previous failed SatVI guess. Thus no third-person possessive is printed on the first word. The summit token is ወድማሑ; second throne ends ReesI, not an invented u suffix. Editorial asterisk immediately before eske and apparatus45-49 are described in notes and excluded from normalized lexical text. ConfidenceLOW is limited to accepted selected-critical-edition scope, not unknown fidels or meanings. No individual source glyph/word meaning remains unresolved in this proposed row. Different Claremont/Toronto physical copies do not add manuscript evidence. V1 and v2 HOLDs remain immutable; this same actor adds no independent vote and no publication approval.
transcription_uncertainties: Accepted only within Charles1906 selected-critical main-line scope. Its printed asterisk and recorded variants are not newly adjudicated against manuscripts; LOW is retained for that honest editorial scope, not invented unknown characters.

translation.text: But the middle one[a] reaches as far as heaven, like a throne for the Lord made of pēkā-stone.[b] And the top of the throne is of sapphire-stone.[c]

footnotes.text: The source has the middle/central adjective with affixed sä (ሰ), a focusing or contrasting particle, not a third-person possessive suffix. But the middle one represents that conjunction-plus-particle construction without adding its, their or a mountain noun. The spatial verb is directly controlled by Dillmann’s attingere with eske (reach/touch as far as), where he cites this verse; the following separate trudere/protrudere sub-sense is not the citation used here.

Pēkā is the printed stone name. Dillmann’s complete photographed1865 Latin entry cites this verse and gives white marble, perhaps alabaster. The historical name is retained without certifying an exact modern mineral identification. Made of supplies English wording for the relative-plus-material-from construction; it describes the throne in the comparison, not the Lord.

This follows the Charles1906 selected critical main line. Literally the latter has its summit, of/for the throne, from sapphire-stone; the la construction names the throne after the anticipatory suffix and is rendered the top of the throne. No his throne or mountain is inserted. Charles places an editorial asterisk immediately before eske (as far as) and records variants in notes45-49; these are not newly collated manuscript evidence. Sapphire is the historical lexical name, not a modern gemological certification.
